title: Avoiding Backfall in Horizontal Drain Lines
description: Proper slope is essential in gravity drainage systems. A common installation mistake is backfall, where a horizontal pipe sags or slopes backward toward the fixture. This creates standing water, traps solid waste, and leads to persistent clogs and sewer odors. Drainage piping must maintain a continuous downward slope according to local plumbing codes to ensure wastewater and solids travel together effectively. Plumbers must use appropriate pipe supports and verify slope with a level before securing permanent hangers.

Avoiding Backfall in Horizontal Drain Lines

Proper slope is essential in gravity drainage systems. A common installation mistake is backfall, where a horizontal pipe sags or slopes backward toward the fixture. This creates standing water, traps solid waste, and leads to persistent clogs and sewer odors. Drainage piping must maintain a continuous downward slope according to local plumbing codes to ensure wastewater and solids travel together effectively. Plumbers must use appropriate pipe supports and verify slope with a level before securing permanent hangers.
